riverbend-music-center: The venue says an ADA-section purchase confirms that someone in the party needs reserved seating because of mobility or standing difficulties. Visitors may be asked to remain seated there during the event.

By purchasing tickets for the ADA section, you confirm that you or a member of your party requires reserved seating due to mobility or standing difficulties. To ensure that all guests enjoy an optimal viewing experience, you may be requested to remain seated in the ADA section throughout the event.
First Aid is at the east end of the property, closest to Belterra Park.

The FAQ permits four unfrozen, factory-sealed non-alcoholic drinks in plastic bottles, or soft empty squeezable plastic water bottles. Water-filling stations are on the concourse. Some shows require drinks to be poured into cups; check the event page on the day.

Patrons are allowed 4 (unfrozen) factory sealed non-alcoholic beverages in plastic bottles for events. Alternatively, patrons can bring in soft, empty, squeezable plastic water bottles. Cups and bottles can be filled up at the ICON Property Water Filling Stations located on the concourse. Please note, the concert you are attending may require you to pour your water bottles into cups. Please refer to your specific event page on the day of show for pour policies. Canned beverages are prohibited.
The box office is beside the main gate. The page checked November 13, 2026 says it is closed for the season; check for reopening information before travelling there to buy tickets.
The Riverbend Music Center and PNC Pavilion box office is closed for the season. Please check back for updates.
The Riverbend Music Center & PNC Pavilion Box Office is located next to the main gate entrance.
The FAQ allows lining up outside the main gate no more than one hour before door time. This is a queue-timing rule, not a promise of seats or shelter while waiting.
You may line up outside the Riverbend Music Center & PNC Pavilion Main Gate entrance up to one hour before door time.
The FAQ permits service animals covered by ADA regulations and prohibits pets and other animals. The reviewed page does not identify a relief area or an assistance procedure.
Service animals covered under ADA Regulations are allowed in the Riverbend Music Center and PNC Pavilion. Pets & other animals are prohibited from all events.
great-american-ball-park: The access guide identifies an elevator entrance at Johnny Bench Way and Mehring Way beside a limited pickup/drop-off area. It does not give the dimensions or full route from the curb.

A limited pickup/drop off zone is located at the corner of Johnny Bench Way and Mehring Way, on the southeast corner of the ballpark. Guests may enter the building through the Elevator Entrance on that corner.
Gate D is reserved for suite holders and is reached by ramp, elevator or escalator. Gate E is open to all guests; both are on the Suite Level.

The majority of Great American Ball Park Entrances are on accessible routes. Gates A, B, C, and H are at street level, while Gates D and E are on the Suite Level. Gate D is accessible to Suite Holders only and can be accessed by ramp, elevator, or escalator. Gate E is accessible to all Guests by ramp, elevator, or escalator.

The access guide lists Braille and tactile signs throughout the ballpark, and closed-captioned game broadcasts on televisions in all club areas. It does not identify a particular seat with a guaranteed view of captions.
Braille and tactile signs are located throughout the facility.
In addition to in-bowl captioning, the Reds will caption the game broadcasts in all club areas of the ballpark through closed captioning on televisions dispersed throughout the club areas.
For an issue needing Public Safety during a visit, the guide says to text REDS and the issue to 69050. Staff reply and are dispatched when needed; message and data charges may apply.

In the event that you have an issue while at Great American Ball Park and need to reach the Public Safety staff, you can text "REDS" and your issue to 69050.
Public Safety will reply, and staff will be dispatched to your area if the situation demands a response.
Message and data rates may apply.

The guide’s First Aid section lists rooms near Terrace sections 109–110 and 125–126 and View section 411, staffed during games and large events. Its wheelchair section instead names 109, 127 and 409. Ask staff for the current nearest room rather than relying on the conflicting section numbers.

TriHealth First Aid Stations are staffed with trained medical personnel affiliated with TriHealth's Bethesda North and Good Samaritan Hospital.
Guests will find the Great American Ball Park First Aid Stations in the following locations:
Terrace Level near Sections 125-126.
On the Terrace Level near Sections 109-110.
View Level near Section 411.
Medical personnel are on duty for all games and large events (i.e. concerts). Should medical assistance be needed, ask any member of the Great American Ball Park staff for immediate assistance or in less serious situations the location of the nearest First Aid Room.

Guests in need of a wheelchair transport can make their request to the nearest Reds Public Safety Employee, either of the two TriHealth Fan Accommodation Stations located at Sections 119 and 420 near Gapper's Alley, or at any of the TriHealth First Aid Stations located near Sections 109, 127 or 409. A Game Day Team member will escort you to your seat and can pick you up when you are ready to leave. Wheelchairs are not available for personal use during the event.

The Reds identify grassy berms outside the re-entry gate by Gate A as a service-animal relief area. Their policy permits service dogs and miniature horses, excludes comfort animals, and requires control by tether or another effective method when disability or the task prevents tethering. Confirm the exit and return procedure with staff.

In accordance with state and federal law, service dogs and miniature horses assisting guests with disabilities are permitted inside Great American Ball Park. Other animals, including comfort animals, are not permitted in Great American Ball Park.
Service dogs must be harnessed, tethered, or leashed, unless those devices interfere with the service dog's work or the Guests disability prevents these devices from being used. In that case, the Guest must maintain control of the dog through voice, signal, or other effective controls.
The grassy berms outside the Re-Entry Gate by Gate A has been designated as the animal relief area.
Reds Staff may ask for your ticket location. While service dogs are permitted, some members of the public are unaware of this. Reds staff will note where you are sitting to prevent other Guests from interfering with the work of the service dog.
paycor-stadium: For game-day seating requests, the guide directs visitors to the North Ticket Office between Northwest and Northeast Gates. Advance ADA-seat purchases remain first come, first served; a same-day change is not guaranteed.

Paycor Stadium has over 1,000 handicap seating areas available. If you have special seating needs, please contact the Bengals ticket office at 513-621-8383. The ticket office is open Monday-Friday from 9 a.m.-5 p.m. On game day, handicap seating can be arranged by visiting the North Ticket office (located between the altafiber Northwest Gate and Northeast Gate on the north end of the stadium).

Accessible (ADA) seating is available throughout Paycor Stadium, on all three levels. Guests who require ADA seating should contact the Bengals ticket office at 513-621-8383 to purchase those seats in advance. Seats are offered on a first come, first served basis.
First Aid stations are listed at East Sideline 136, West Sideline 116, North Plaza 129, East Canopy 334 and West Canopy 316. For an emergency, notify a stadium team member.

First Aid stations are located throughout the stadium at the following locations:
East Sideline - Section 136
West Sideline - Section 116
North Plaza - Section 129
East Canopy - Section 334
West Canopy - Section 316

For any medical emergency while inside Paycor Stadium, notify any Paycor Stadium Team Member, who will contact medical assistance. If patrons know in advance that they may need to exit Paycor Stadium for a medical emergency, they may register at the Kettering Health First Aid Station located on the plaza level in the north endzone closest to Northeast Gate.

For pumping equipment, notify security at the ticket gate so the bag can be screened and tagged. Nursing/pumping spaces are at sections 114 and 144; Kettering Health First Aid stations can also provide a private space with electricity if needed.

Nursing mothers who would like to bring in pumping equipment can do so by approaching the ticket gate and notifying our security personnel. Security will screen your bag and tag it so that it can be permitted to enter.
Once inside the stadium, if you would like to nurse or pump, please find your way to one of our dedicated nursing stations located at section 114 or 144 or any one of our Kettering Health First Aid stations where they can provide you with a clean, private space with electricity (if needed).

The Bengals warn that cheering, noise and standing are normal during games and may temporarily block sightlines. Their standing policy asks fans to consider people who cannot stand; it does not guarantee an unobstructed seated view.

The Jungle is celebrated for its energy and noise, which are important to the home field atmosphere and broader live sporting event experience. Guests should be aware that standing, cheering, and expressive reactions are common during gameplay, which may temporarily impact sightlines for some guests. This applies for fans of both teams.
By attending an event, ticket holders acknowledge and accept that:
Standing is a normal and expected part of the live game experience
Clear views may vary depending on game action and crowd behavior
Situations in which standing is permitted include but are not limited to:
Big plays – interceptions, defensive stops on 3rd and 4th downs, sacks, general things that excite fans during games
Any points scored – touchdown, field goal
Pre-snap for defensive snaps
Otherwise, the majority rules. Fans are asked to be considerate of others nearby, who may have a limited ability to stand and view the game.
For problems during Bengals games, text HELP to 69050 with the problem and location, as directed by the fan guide.

Fans wishing to report poor behavior or other concerns during Bengals games at Paycor Stadium may do so by sending the text message "HELP" to 69050 with your problem and location. Patrons who fail to comply with the Fan Code of Conduct may be ejected and have their season tickets revoked. More serious offenses could lead to arrest.
The fan guide checked November 13, 2026 says stadium tours are unavailable because of 2026 construction projects. It does not give a reopening date.

We are currently in the process of continuing to make improvements to Paycor Stadium to ensure it provides a best-in-class experience for fans. Due to 2026 construction projects, stadium tours are currently not available.
